title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE will be more expensive than its predecessor, here's by how much
description: A few hours ago the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE was certified with support for 45W wired charging just like its predecessor, and now there's a leak telling us how much it will cost in Europe - specifically in France. title: Counterpoint: Global smartphone chipset shipments down 15% in first half of 2026
description: Smartphone shipments have been on the decline for the past few months as the ongoing memory chip shortage continues to plague OEMs. And as you can imagine, other components are getting hit too. Take smartphone chipsets, for example. According to the latest Counterpoint Research report, global smartphone chipset shipments have declined by 15% during the first half of 2026. The two biggest players – Qualcomm and MediaTek have been hit the worst, with an estimated 25% decline in SoC shipments compared to H1 2025. description: AT&T has now announced that it has finalized its acquisition of $23 billion worth of spectrum licenses from EchoStar. The transaction was announced back in August of last year. AT&T paid all that money for an average of approximately 50MHz of low-band and mid-band spectrum that covers "virtually every market across the US", more than 400 in total. There's 30MHz of 3.45GHz mid-band spectrum in there as well as 20MHz of 600MHz low-band spectrum. And there's more still; apparently, the rogue AI then accessed Modal through one of its customers' exploits, and then used Modal Labs as a stepping stone to carry out its attacks on Hugging Face. description: Samsung unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold8, Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip8 last week, and then started taking pre-orders for them. Apple will task Samsung Display as the exclusive supplier for the touchscreen OLED panels. title: Samsung Galaxy S26 FE's charging speed revealed via new certification
description: The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE - expected to arrive in September - has been spotted on the UL Demko certification database, revealing its charging speed. The listing mentions 15V/3A and 10V/4.5A charging ratings, indicating the S26 FE supports a maximum charging speed of 45W. That's the same as last year's Galaxy S25 FE and this year's Galaxy S26+, but slower than the Galaxy S26 Ultra (60W) and faster than the Galaxy S26 (25W).
